messages.author: 7da7896d9f19f510
messages.subject: background with colored x-ranges
parts:
Appreciate any thoughts you have on how to do this:

Plotting a time series, I want to deliniate multiple time ranges (the x axis) with a colored background extending the height of the graph. By modifying the theme panel.background somehow? Would also be helpful if I can add labels to that range that are drawn either within the plot or at the top.

Or maybe another R package does this easier?

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: background with colored x-ranges
parts:
Hi:

Failing a reproducible example, here's a modified version of a plot
from the ggplot2 book that has similar characteristics to what you
describe.

# Example using unemployment data from the economics data frame
# and the presidential data frame in the ggplot2 package

library(ggplot2)

# Monthly time series plot of unemployment rate
ggplot(economics, aes(x = date, y = unemploy)) +
geom_line() +
labs(x = "", y = "No. unemployed (1000s)")

# Data on presidential terms over this time span
presterms <- presidential[-(1:2), ]

# Generated data to use for labeling terms
presmidterm <- data.frame(name = presterms$name, midterm =
with(presterms, as.Date((as.numeric(start) + as.numeric(end))/2,
origin = "1970-01-01")),
stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
presmidterm$name[1] <- "Johnson"

ggplot() +
theme_bw() +
geom_rect(data = presterms, aes(xmin = start, xmax = end,
ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = party), alpha = 0.3) +
geom_line(data = economics, aes(x = date, y = unemploy)) +
labs(x = "", y = "No. unemployed (1000s)") +
geom_text(data = presmidterm, aes(x = midterm, y = 2500, label = name),
size = 3) +
scale_fill_manual(values = c("blue", "red"))



Dennis

messages.subject: Re: background with colored x-ranges
parts:
Hi,

I was able to use the post from Dennis as follows:

# Input Data ----
dt.a = seq(as.Date("2012/1/1"), by = "day", to = as.Date("2012/12/31"))
i.len = length(dt.a)
prepaid.rev = round(sample(rnorm(n=2*i.len,mean=100,sd=10),size=i.len,replace=F),2)
postpaid.rev = round(sample(rnorm(n=2*i.len,mean=50,sd=20),size=i.len,replace=F),2)
total.rev = prepaid.rev + postpaid.rev

df.1 = data.frame(dt = dt.b, prepaid=prepaid.rev,postpaid=postpaid.rev,total=total.rev)
# `````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````

# Basic Graphs ----
ggplot(df.1, aes(x=dt,y=prepaid)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  labs(x = "", y = "PrePaid Revenue (1000s)") 

ggplot(df.1, aes(x=dt,y=postpaid)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  labs(x = "", y = "PostPaid Revenue (1000s)") 

ggplot(df.1, aes(x=dt,y=total)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  labs(x = "", y = "Total Revenue (1000s)") 
# `````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````

# Data Preperation for Background Ranges ----
dt.b = seq(as.Date("2012/1/1"), by = "month", length.out = 12)

# Last Day of Each Month
dt.c = dt.b - 1

# Correcting First Entry
dt.c = dt.c[-1]
dt.c[12] = dt.b[12] + 30

mon = c("Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun","Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec")

# Alternate bands
i.fill = rep(x=c(1,2),times=6)

df.bgd = data.frame(mon=mon,start =dt.b,end = dt.c, i.fill = i.fill)

# For label placement, mid month
df.bgd$mid = with(df.bgd, as.Date((as.numeric(start) + as.numeric(end))/2, 
                      origin = "1970-01-01"))
# `````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````

# Final Plot ----
ggplot() + 
  theme_bw() + 
  geom_rect(data = df.bgd, aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, 
                                  ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,fill=i.fill), alpha = 0.2) + 
  geom_line(data =df.1, aes(x=dt,y=prepaid),col="blue") +
  geom_line(data =df.1, aes(x=dt,y=postpaid),col="red") + 
  labs(x = "", y = "Revenue (1000s)") +  
  geom_text(data = df.bgd, aes(x = mid, y = -5, label = mon), 
          size = 3) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# `````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````````

Requesting further help with the following:

1. How to remove x-axis labels, though I specify "" below:
  labs(x = "", y = "Revenue (1000s)") +  

2. How to remove white bands in the plot extending beyond the specified range i.e. Before Jan-12 and After Dec-12
Output attached as PDF

If I read your request properly, add this to the last line of your final plot:

scale_x_date(breaks = NULL, expand = c(0, 0))

Dennis
